camera.status: built, ungated — 2,497 lines in 10 files plus a 739-line, 114-check selftest (wired as pnpm test:game-camera). Owns no world state, no entity kind and no sim half: stats() reports 0 meshes and 0 materials, and world.modules has no camera key. Drives the renderer's ArcRotateCamera rather than making its own, so the DefaultRenderingPipeline and SSAO2 stay bound; it ADOPTS an outside write instead of snapping back, which is what a showcase's direct camera write tests. Presets are content (cameraPresets pack category, claimed — unclaimedPackKeys() is []), authored in bearing/pitch and derived into alpha/beta, and the module publishes horizonRow(pitch, fov, height) — the arithmetic that would have caught the two rounds core spent reading a sky out of a frame that could not contain one. All seven presets photographed at 12:00 plus night at 23:00 plus the three showcase presets, 0 console errors, 0 warnings, 0 hydration warnings. The pose lives in localStorage, never in a save, and is skipped under ?harness=1.

track.status: built, ungated — 5,495 lines in 21 files. C2 cubic spline through a tridiagonal solve (not Catmull-Rom: a C1 interpolant puts a curvature jump at every knot and curvature is what a rider feels), rotation-minimising roll gauge, the spline IS the heartline 1.1 m above the rails. Ten primitive ops are the only switch in the module and it switches on the instruction set; 19 elements are DATA on top of them, with op arguments as expressions parsed by a hand-written parser rather than Function(), because packs load from URLs. Physics is a fixed-delta-s energy march. selftest.mjs: 95 checks, now wired into pnpm test:game.

shops.status: built, ungated — 6,170 lines in 13 files. Sim: a queue per shop, a till per counter, stock, deliveries, takings, refusals, staffing demand, and find(need, x, z, cash) ranked by walk + wait in park minutes. Main: one parametric building generator (five massings), a 4x2 procedural PBR atlas, thin instances, a night-light pool. Measured: 12 shop types = 25 meshes / 19,094 triangles, and the draw calls are per TYPE not per shop — a park with eight burger stands costs what one costs. In the demo park 7 shops = 1.4 % of the 1,200 draw-call budget and 0.83 % of the frame. Sim tick 0.0007 ms. 51-check selftest, now wired as pnpm test:game-shops.

openIssues: camera, found and fixed during verification: the module inherited the renderer's opening pose (93.7 m up, 33.75 degrees down, horizonRow -138), so /game opened on a park with the horizon off the top of the frame and no sky in it. Invisible in every screenshot taken so far because the harness always applies a preset. main() now applies `overview` when there is nothing remembered to restore: 105.8 m, 15.5 degrees down, horizonRow 153.3. A remembered view, a showcase's direct write and ?cam= each still win over it, verified after the change.

OPEN (camera showcase, terrain's side): the `leash-out` preset — the camera at the target leash looking away from the park — shows the world ending on the SHOWCASE landscape: the terrain patch's edge stands as a cliff and the water slab is cut off in mid-air. The demo park passes the same test because its apron runs to 1,756 m and the far edge fades into haze before the dome. So it is the showcase generator's finite patch, not the leash, and it belongs to terrain.

OPEN (terrain): `/game?showcase=camera` and `/game?showcase=terrain` both log the identical pair of `WebGL: INVALID_VALUE: bufferSubData: buffer overflow` warnings — the camera module does nothing in the second, so they come from `generateShowcaseLandscape` writing back into a vertex buffer sized for the previous mesh. Two warnings, no errors, nothing visibly wrong in the frames.

OPEN (camera, stated by the module): nobody has driven this camera with a hand. Pan, orbit, zoom, momentum and edge scroll are covered by 900 frames of synthetic input in the selftest and by nothing else, because a headless harness has no mouse. Follow mode has never followed anything that moves either — `trains` does not exist and the `track:` stand-in was not photographed.

CLOSED (guests round 2): the two models of buying are one. `guests` now calls `shops.find(need, x, z, cash)`, walks to the OFFER's frontage rather than the entity position, `join`s the queue, stands where `place()` says while it waits, `collect`s a receipt or `leave`s as a balk, and `lastRefusal` explains a refusal instead of the guest silently wandering off. Verified by the integrator over a full demo-park day at speed 5, and it agrees to the cent three ways: cash delta 273,550 = guests.spentToday 273,550 = shops.takingsToday 273,550. A/B on the same seed: 292 sales / EUR 2,165.50 / longest line 0 before, 534 / EUR 2,735.50 / longest line 9 after, plus 415 price refusals and 2 balks that used to be silent. The old venue model stays as the branch taken when no `shops` module answered — a showcase loads five modules, not twenty-four — and a 48-hour soak with `shops` dropped from the list is 0 stuck, 0 errors, and still trades.

A FOURTH unsaved accumulator in `guests`, found in round 2 and fixed: `Venue.incoming`, the soft reservation `scoreVenue` divides by, was rebuilt to zero on every load, so the first plan after a resume was scored against an empty park. That makes four — the RNG streams, the gate's party debt, the thought cursor and now this — every one found by a field-by-field diff of two serialisations rather than by reading.

STILL OPEN (guests round 2, its own weakest point, stated): 534 sales a day across seven shops is six per shop per hour, so lines run 0-9 park-wide. The cause is the distance term — `speed` is metres per PARK minute, so a shop 60 m away is a 43-minute walk and `scoreVenue` divides its worth by 5.8. That is the D-006 time-compression tension the file already documents, not the shops bridge.

STILL OPEN (paths, found by the guests round-2 diff): ten position columns still differ after a save + one tick, because `TREES_PER_TICK = 2` and a warm 64-entry LRU mean a resumed park falls through to the greedy neighbour step. Pre-existing — HEAD diverges at the same tick in MORE columns — and written up with three candidate fixes in docs/game/requests/guests.md section 1.

GUESTS BUG, found by the shops builder because it had to explain why nobody was buying anything, and confirmed: needs did not rise at ANY speed a player can select. `d.needs` was a Uint8Array written through Math.round, and the per-tick rise is 0.0217 units at speed 1, 0.065 at 3, 0.108 at 5 and 0.217 at 10 — every one rounds to zero. It moves only at 100x, which is the speed the SOAK runs at, so the one test exercising this module ran at the single speed where the bug is invisible. Measured before: 934 of 944 guests idle with no destination after three park hours, mean hunger 24 against urgentAt 170. After widening the column to Float32: mean hunger 115.6 / 116.0 / 115.8 at speeds 1/3/5 after 300 park minutes, identical across speeds, which is what a time-based decay must be. A save written before the widening still loads (u8 read and widened).

HARNESS: `game-shot.mjs --step=N` used to die with 'Resulting promise was garbage collected' under SwiftShader — reproducible four runs of four on `--cam=overview`, and adding the shops to the demo park made `ground` do it too. `waitForFunction` installs a long-lived promise in the page and a scene heavy enough to stall the render loop gets it collected. It polls from node in short evaluates now.

demo-park now places its shops: 7 of 8 planned plots filled, chosen by NEED against the registry rather than by pack id, at x = +/-11 because the street's lamps are at +/-6.2, its limes at +/-8 and the path graph's service radius is 14 m. The eighth plot (a second happiness shop at 26, 186) is empty because the bundled packs have only one — the code leaves a plot empty rather than inventing a shop for it.

CORE BUG, found by the guests module being photographed: a step control that does nothing while paused. `SimRuntime.tick()` computes dt from clock.speed and skips its whole body at dt <= 0, so the worker's `step` message ran the scheduler over a world that stood still. The screenshot harness runs at speed=0 for repeatability, so every frame of the guests module photographed an empty avenue with 'Guests 0' in the HUD. `runtime.step()` forces one tick at speed 1 now — the only reading of 'one tick' that does not depend on a speed the caller deliberately set to zero — and game-shot.mjs takes --step=N.

guests: `destKind` was declared on GuestStore and allocated nowhere. `allocate` builds the store with `as unknown as GuestStore`, so the compiler was told the column existed and never checked, and grow/zero/serialize/load each listed their byte columns by hand and each missed the same one. Every tick threw. Fixed with a BYTE_FIELDS list the five sites share, a GuestColumn union the type is checked against, and a runtime guard that names an unallocated column.

guests: THREE unsaved accumulators broke save -> resume, and a field-by-field diff of two serialisations found them. The four xoshiro streams were the obvious one; the gate's fractional party debt and the thought scanner's cursor and budget were not. The debt made the first guest to arrive after a save come in at park minute 2006 in the uninterrupted run and 2006.25 in the resumed one — one tick — with the people, their ids and their slots identical. The diff is zero fields now.

STILL OPEN (guests): there is nothing in the park to WANT. No shops, no rides, no toilets — those modules do not exist — so every need runs to its critical threshold and stays there, and the interesting half of this module is untested against real demand. And the crowd bunches into tight knots on the fountain square, which may simply be the wayfinding funnelling everyone down one lane; the lane offset has never been tuned against a park with destinations in it.

CORRECTION to something this file carried for three rounds: the world's edge fix recorded here as 'more apron, or a distance fade' was half WRONG. The terrain critic measured that the apron already runs to 1,756 m and projects to screen row 188, while the visible step is at row 231 and 900 m out — which is DOME_RADIUS in sky-dome.ts. More apron cannot help; 1,600 of the surround's 3,840 triangles are already permanently occluded by the dome. Planting needs 28-52 m, not the 65 m estimated earlier. The one lever that works is a distance fade in the fragment injection point terrain already owns; the fog alternative needs 2.9x the density and is environment's.

terrain round 2: extensibility was 4.0, UNDER the 5.0 floor — the first hard-gate failure in this gauntlet. The module touched registry/pack/manifest nowhere at all and its ground catalogue was a switch over indices with 21 colour constants beside it. Ground layers are a manifest now, split the way paths already splits: the PATTERN is an algorithm and stays in code, the colours and relief are data. A pack can retint a built-in in place (by id, so a save's paint indices keep meaning) or add one past the built-ins; a bad recipe is named and skipped. LAYER_COUNT stays 7 and that limit is written down. Pinned by pnpm test:game-registry.

terrain round 2: the shadow proxy was 33.9 % of the whole frame — stride 2 over a 256-cell heightfield is 32,768 triangles rendered once per cascade, 98,304 of the demo park's 290,262 at overview. The critic proved it twice (render list 75.6 % proxy; showcase 141,340 at noon against 43,038 at 18:30, a difference of 98,302). Stride 4 now (3 on ultra): 290,262 -> 216,534 triangles, -73,728, -25.4 %, at an unchanged 145 draw calls, and the frame is indistinguishable.

This also corrects the demo-park critique, which blamed a 17-degree cut slope on a planting refusal: nothing refuses to plant at 17 degrees, scatter.ts fades from 38.7.

The `paths` selftest was RED at HEAD in four runs of four while the module's report claimed '25 assertions, all passing'. Nothing ran it — it was not in pnpm test:game. It is `pnpm test:game-paths` now, and the assertion is the PER-QUERY time (0.313 us idle, threshold 2 us) rather than a total that depends on the query count. paths round 2: exactly ONE lamp reached the paving, at medium, high AND ultra, where the night rig's pool holds two, four and six — the disparity widened the more the machine could afford. mesh.lightSources sorts by renderPriority and a PBR material takes the first maxSimultaneousLights, so with four slots the list was [sun, sky, env-moon-light, lamp-0]: TWO of the four slots on the largest surface in the frame went to lights at intensity 0.000 at 22:00. Six now, matching scenery and track. Zero draw calls, zero triangles, and .game-render/pn/2200-ground.png is the first lit avenue in this project.

paths round 2: a pack carrying `pathStyles` registered, was reported by unclaimedPackKeys(), and changed nothing — registerPathStyle had no caller and the docblock above it said the seam was waiting for core. Core landed that; attachPathStyles closes it and claims both `pathStyles` and `pathMaterials`. Pinned by pnpm test:game-registry: 6 -> 7 styles from a manifest, surface recipe resolving with it, unclaimed keys [].

paths round 2: `path-concrete-slab` was one colour with a grid drawn on it — the exact thing textures.ts opens by saying the per-cell tint prevents. SLAB_M is 1 m and the recipe tiled at 2 m, so the texture held FOUR slabs and repeated every two metres; the albedo read back off the GPU spanned 5.5 of 255, 2.9 %. Four metres and a per-slab tint at 1.15 now. Cobble at 27.4 across 18x18 is the standard it aims at.

STILL OPEN (paths, all measured by its critic, none fixed): 50.4 % of the module's triangles are KERB (24,243 of 48,144, 5.05x the surface it edges); no LOD and no spatial split, so those 48,144 are identical across all six camera x time rows and 16.6 % of the overview frame; graph rebuild 11.2-12.9 ms against a 6 ms whole-sim budget; texture generation 3,784.8 ms at `high`; no camber, crossfall or drainage anywhere, two vertices across an eight-metre avenue; two orphan kerb fragments inside a junction cap.

scenery round 2: the far foliage imposter drew a RECTANGLE for both species. An earlier critic had called it species-blind; it branches per species and always did — what both branches shared was `addCard`, which draws a quad, so a spruce was a rectangle and a broadleaf a disc of leaves above a bare stick, i.e. a palm. At `overview` 1,289 of the demo park's 1,290 trees are drawn this way, so those few vertices are what the whole mid-ground looks like. `addCard` takes a silhouette `profile` now. Costed by the critic before it was written: widening the LOD break to draw real trees there costs 263,000 triangles and doubles the frame; the profile cost 18,648 (+6.2 %) at unchanged draw calls.

scenery round 2: the triangle allocation was upside down and neither earlier critic saw it. At `ground`, meadow-flowers took 154,848 triangles (35.9 %) of the module's 431,300 and hedge-box 73,364 — 62 % on ground cover against 16 % for all 1,344 trees. At `overview`, hedge-box alone was 29,184 of 79,490 (36.7 %) for 76 one-metre hedges at 340 m, more than every tree in frame. Both now collapse at LOD 2. Net at overview INCLUDING the tree fix: 299,646 -> 290,262 triangles (-9,384) at an unchanged 145 draw calls.

scenery round 2: a pack registered after boot never reached the module — buildCatalog ran once, so registering a pack took registry.items('foliage') 7 -> 9 while the module's catalogue stayed at 26 with every new key null. Nothing subscribed to registry.onPack. A pack from loadPackFromUrl was invisible to the one module whose job is drawing content. Fixed; detaches in dispose.

The two-lamps question is SETTLED and both earlier critics were right: 74 light sites, 72 lamp entities, POOL_BY_PRESET.medium = 2. Both pool lights run at 63.0 at 22:00 and light bench, hedge and grass; no lamp puts a pool on PAVING. Mechanism: all eight path-* materials and terrain-ground carry maxSimultaneousLights = 4 while scenery's carry 6, the scene holds five lights, and lamps sit at renderPriority = -1. Raising the pool is only half the fix; the path materials' light budget is the other half and belongs to `paths`.

CORE BUG, found by the environment critic by DIFFING PNGs rather than reading code, fixed: `?weather=rain` rendered a clear noon. `core/host.ts` wrote `{ weather, forced }` into `world.modules.environment` — a shape it invented — while both halves of the environment module read `slot.kind`, so the flag was accepted, stored and ignored. The rain frame differed from the clear one by 123 of 2,764,800 bytes at `close` and by ZERO at `ground`. The in-game path had always worked, because it goes through the module's command. Core now dispatches `environment:weather` instead of writing another module's state; verified from the URL afterwards at fogDensity 0.000845 and env-rain at 1,385 live particles. Every screenshot of rain, storm or snow taken by anybody on this branch before this was a screenshot of a clear day.

environment round 2: the weather fog was not held to the arithmetic the clear-day fog is. At the rain values it put half a surface's contrast into haze at 447 m — worse than the 660 m the module's own comment condemns as fog on a clear day. The rain term is scaled by `intensity` now, so a shower and a storm differ by more than their particles. Measured half-contrast: clear 1,525 m, overcast 771 m, rain 664 m, storm 605 m.

STILL OPEN (environment): auto exposure is pinned at EXPOSURE_MAX = 3.600 at 18:30 AND 22:00. At night that is by design; at dusk it means no metering at the hour a sky model is most worth metering. Across weather at noon it is not pinned (clear 1.954, rain 2.959, storm 3.342, overcast 3.496) — but an overcast noon still renders 1.79x a clear one, right for a camera and wrong for reading weather off a frame.

STILL OPEN (environment): twilight crosses through GREEN (132/144/130 at y=230, G above R and B) because Preetham has no ozone term — Chappuis-band absorption is exactly what keeps a real twilight blue instead of passing through green between a warm horizon and a cold zenith. That is a change to the scattering model, not to a constant. And the IBL's ground hemisphere is a knife-edge terminator on the showcase's own mirror ball.

Three claims in the environment report were measured FALSE by its critic and are corrected in place: '88 % at 340 m' is 96.9 % (88 % is at 689 m, the figure was read off the wrong distance); the shoulder's blue:red pair 2.81/3.70 reproduces as 3.19/4.23 because the sample azimuth was never stated; and 'the park is black, no light rigs exist' was wrong — two scenery-lamp-* lights run at 22:00 and are visibly lit.

CORE BUG, found by the track critic by probing rather than reading, fixed: `packManifestSchema` was a plain `z.object()`, which STRIPS unknown keys — so NO module could ever own a content category of its own. The track module's `trackElements` was deleted before any consumer saw it (`'trackElements' in parsed === false`, and the onPack listener got the stripped copy too), and `registerTrackElementsFromPack` had zero call sites on top of that. The manifest passes unknown keys through now; `registerPackCategory(category, owner)` lets a module claim one (the counterpart to registerKind, one level up) and `unclaimedPackKeys()` reports the rest, so a typo is a named line instead of a silent empty array. Proven end to end and pinned by pnpm test:game-registry: 21 -> 22 elements from a manifest with no TypeScript, and `trackElments` reported by name.

track round 2: bracing is tiered and no bay is skipped. It used to put ONE X per bay whatever its height, and skipped every second timber bay under a comment claiming that is how a real wooden coaster is braced — it is not; a woodie's bents stand 3-4 m apart and every bay between them is braced. Measured like for like at the `close` camera: 772,548 -> 903,924 triangles (+17 %) at an unchanged 90 draw calls.

STILL OPEN (track, its own #1 and the tier cap's reason): the wooden structure aliases into a dark smear at the `overview` camera, and more members make it worse. The honest fix is a distance LOD that swaps the lattice for a coarser silhouette. Not built.

The account session limit has now killed a fan-out TWICE: 22 agents at xhigh (0 done, 22 errored) and then 3 agents (a demo-park round-2 builder and two critics, all three dead on the same 429). So the ceiling is TOKEN THROUGHPUT, not agent count, and the working assumption is at most one or two subagents at a time — or the integrator does the work in-session, which is how demo-park round 2 was done.

demo-park round 2 (integrator, not a builder): planting now follows the circulation. Trees 893 -> 1,196; within 10 m of a path 6.9 % -> 16.2 %; the 80-120 m band 7.8 -> 46.6 trees/ha, so the bathtub profile the round-1 critic measured is gone. 34 % more trees cost 0 draw calls (145, unchanged) and 1.5 % more triangles, because scenery instances them. 16.2 % rather than 30 % is deliberate and argued in the report: the proxy can be gamed by pulling every setback under 10 m, which would close the canopy over three four-metre loops.

STILL OPEN (track, its own #1): at 340 m a timber member is 0.26 m of real width against roughly 0.5 m per pixel, so 556 columns and their bracing sub-pixel-alias into a dark smear at the `overview` camera. Bracing alternate bays halved the member count and it is still visible. Needs a distance LOD that swaps the lattice for a coarser silhouette; the preset offers no MSAA. Confirmed by the integrator on `.game-render/track-verify/1200-overview.png` — the three layouts read as coaster shapes, the structure reads as speckle.

STILL OPEN (track): supports are vertical only, so any stretch rolled past 78 degrees gets none — a vertical column would meet the underside edge-on. On the three demo layouts this hits the corkscrew and the top of the loop, which are correctly unsupported in reality too, so nothing floats; a heavily overbanked layout would show gaps.

STILL OPEN (track): a layout is tuned for its train and nothing warns you. The ops shape themselves from a running-speed estimate that reads the train's drag area and rolling resistance, so a car 5 cm narrower builds a different track — two of three layouts closed 5 m worse under a hand-written train spec. A build tool that lets a player swap the train on an existing layout needs a rebuild-and-recheck API that does not exist.

`nextEntityId` kept a process-global `let idCounter` folded in with the world's own `__ids` by a `Math.max`, so the SECOND world built in a process carried on from where the first stopped — the same seed minted `path-1…` once and `path-4…` the next time (measured). Found by the demo-park builder, which builds its park twice to prove it reproduces. Fixed in core: the sequence lives in the world and nowhere else, and `test-game-save-roundtrip` now builds two worlds and compares, which was verified to FAIL with the counter put back.

STILL OPEN, measured: every tree in the `overview` frame is a LOD 2 imposter and the mid-ground reads as a palm grove — `linden:l2v0` x179, `spruce:l2v0` x351, `oak:l2v0` x288, and no LOD 0 tree mesh has an instance at that camera. At 42 m the same trees are convincing oaks with bark and branching. The break is at the pack's `lod[0] x 0.85 = 34 m`. It is scenery's `gen-foliage.ts` to fix; the demo park is where it shows.
Draw calls: 145 at `overview`, peak 237 at `ground` — 19.8 % of the 1,200 whole-game budget with six modules unbuilt, and roughly 127 of the 237 are shadow-map passes.

The sky, the fog and the exposure were all wrong in the same direction and are measured now. Three causes, each verified against a frame: (1) `scene.fogColor` was written as a LINEAR radiance, and Babylon runs `Color3.toLinearSpaceToRef` over it for every PBR material (`BindFogParameters`, `linearSpace` set), so the shader saw 0.034 where 0.295 was written — distant terrain got DARKER with distance instead of paler (sRGB 58/80/42 unfogged against 46/58/44 at 700 m). (2) The DOME painted `SkyState.ground` below the horizon, which is a term the IBL needs and the backdrop must not have: at the overview camera the terrain's far edge sits ~75 px under the true horizon and those 75 px were a dark olive band, sRGB 24/26/18 against the 75 the horizon ring rendered. That band is what several rounds of screenshots read as 'black above the horizon'. It is haze now — the azimuth's own horizon colour carried straight down, which is also the colour the fog takes the terrain to, so the edge dissolves instead of stepping. (3) The clear-day fog density was 0.0008, which with EXP2 plus Babylon's `toLinearSpace(fog)` put half the contrast of a surface 660 m away into the haze: a visibility of ~1.5 km on a day the model calls clear. 0.00035 now.

Auto exposure was a stop under and is 1.85x: EXPOSURE_KEY 0.42 -> 0.78, MIN 0.55 -> 1.0, MAX 2.2 -> 3.6. Those numbers were set against a frame in which the dome rendered black and the fog was four times too dark, so the scene they were metered against was not this scene. Measured at the old values: exposure settled at 1.054 and sunlit grass came out at 0.069 scene-linear, sRGB 80, where a photograph puts it near 120. Pinning exposure by hand and looking: 2.6 washes the grass towards yellow, 2.0 reads as a clear day.

The sky's shoulder ran per channel and therefore desaturated everything it touched — the horizon measured R:G:B 0.80 : 0.94 : 1.00 off the model and rendered grey. It runs on luminance now and scales all three channels by one factor. Measured on the model at noon, blue:red went 1.54 -> 2.81 at dy 0.3 and 2.05 -> 3.70 at dy 0.6, with the levels unchanged.

STILL OPEN, measured: the sky's horizon:zenith luminance ratio is about 4.5:1 where a real clear sky is nearer 2:1. That is Preetham's own horizon overshoot (it integrates an infinite air path with no ground and no aerosol scale-height cutoff), not the tone curve — lowering SKY_WHITE to fix it caps the sun's halo at 1.16x the horizon and flattens every sunset. The two candidate remedies are attenuating the near-horizon in-scattering in the model, or a separate curve for the solar lobe. Not attempted; SKY_GAIN stays 0.09.

STILL OPEN: at the overview camera the terrain's far edge is now a hard silhouette against the sky, because the fog that used to hide it was fog. The world simply ends about a kilometre out. That is the terrain module's geometry (world size, or a distant skirt), not the environment module's haze.

The camera fallback presets were wrong twice and are fixed twice: `overview` looked 37 degrees down against a 25.8-degree half-FOV, so the horizon was 11.3 degrees OUT of frame and no screenshot of that preset could contain sky; the correction to 23.5 degrees left 36 px of it, so every 'sky' screenshot after that was really a screenshot of the haze band. It is 15.5 degrees now, horizon at 154 px of 720.

20 of 24 modules are scaffolds: paths, pools, track, buildings, scenery, shops, rides, flumes, trains, guests, staff, management, overlays, tools, camera, scenarios, persistence, audio, effects, demo-park. The demo park renders an empty green hill: 47-74 draw calls, 31k-140k triangles.
No glTF assets are fetched by default; every module must look good procedurally and that is graded, not assumed.
The 48-park-hour soak runs 576 ticks at 100x; once guests exist it should also run at a lower speed for more integration steps per park-hour.
No critic gate has run, for this module or any other. The environment frames above are the integrator's own measurements, not a grade.
